reviews.text: Fantastic little gem of a game. It's loads of fun and has the feel of playing a mage down. It's also far more polished than I expected for an EA release. You have access to 3 mages. Fire is unlocked off the bat and you can unlock Frost and Arcane later down the road (I had enough gold left over from playing the test to get Arcane unlocked). Lightning is also there but marked for a later release. Each mage has a set of skills, some of which are locked and require gold to unlock. There's a test dummy right next to the skill selection for you to figure out which mix of abilities works best for you. There are also permanent unlocks for you to work towards that do things like boost base spell damage, crit rate, number of dashes, etc. The combat is chaotic and fun. It starts out slow and really amps up. You'll pick your map and difficulty get dropped in to find a mess of enemies that will just keep coming. The do a good job at hunting you down and they have decent aim too. If you expect to run in a straight line or camp out somewhere, you'll be dead before you know it. Keep moving. As you kill you'll gain XP. When you level you'll be able to pick a card which will augment your play somehow. You can unlock the ability to reroll the cards as well. By far my favorite card sets it so all future cards are picked for you at random. It really adds some spice to a run. There's also powerups that spawn throughout the map. Some much easier to get to than others. Enemies can, if you select the right card, drop HP potions, etc. After killing x number of enemies you'll spawn a boss crystal which when clicked, summons the maps big baddie. The boss fights have some unique mechanics to deal with that give it that bullet hell feeling, plus normal enemies spawning in. If you die you'll sacrifice a chunk of your earned gold but fear not, you have a chance to go back in the stage and recover it... but if you die before getting over to it, it's gone for good. It does need some work on optimization. It's running hotter on my card (2080 Super) than stuff like Space Marine 2 or FF XVI. tl;dr - Amazing find. Great little roguelike that'll give you hours of fun. Plenty of options to customize your mage to fit your playstyle. Neat looking animations, enemies, and spell effects. It's a huge bang for your buck. Can't wait to see what they do with it...

[b][i]A fast-paced first-person arena shooter with roguelike and RPG elements. Destroy monsters and bosses in various locations of the multiverse to unlock and improve your magical powers.[/i][/b] Gameplay: https://youtu.be/assOI0o53r4 You start the game in the hub. Here you can unlock new heroes, choose and improve permanent magic spells. To upgrade your mage, you need to earn gold. You enter one of nine portals, choose a difficulty level and complete current tasks: kill a certain number of enemies, activate a summoning stone and defeat the boss. During the battle, your mage gains experience and levels up. When the mage gains a new level, you are given a choice of three random spell cards. The mage's level and spell cards are active only while you are in this location. When you return to the hub, this upgrade disappears, but your hero has permanent magical powers and gold to upgrade them. + Fun, dynamic gameplay. + Gorgeous, bright graphics. + Excellent music and sounds. + Good optimization. + 9 portal-locations. + 4 difficulty levels. + Various monsters. + Epic bosses. + 4 unlockable heroes: fire, ice, arcane and lightning mage. + Passive and active spells. This is a gem of a game! HOWEVER, and take this realistically, it is incomplete and it is starting to seem like it could be abandoned. Either that, or a long hiatus. For what it has now, it's still fun and a nice brain-off experience with some challenge. The upgrades are addicting, albeit very limited right now. Still this simplicity isn't a bad thing. Plays and runs well, sound is relatively fine, looks good overall, and the roguelite element is placed nicely. You can cheese bosses like no tomorrow with the pickups. Most maps are pretty good and discernable, however one map is completely unfinished and very much noticable. I wouldn't say it's very difficult, but it can provide some challenge. The main issue here is that it is noticeably incomplete with a long pause of updates. They've responded and said that a major update is in the works but it's taking some time, but it's been a few months now. I'd still recommend this for the price and ease of play, but just know that it may not see the end result.

That being said, it's only 6 bucks and you can easily get your money's worth out of it even if the dev decides to just abandon this like the last game. It's fun, and cool, and i hope the dev does work on it, It has a fun game loop, and it has 4 mages as of right now. I hope if it does keep getting worked on, the dev adds multiplayer at some point because it would be very fun to play with friends. As of right now its more than worth it's price and you'll get your gameplay out of it.
